WASHINGTON — At this year’s Farm Progress Show in Boone, Iowa, U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins announced the USDA Data Modernization Plan designed to put farmers first, reduce unnecessary burdens on producers, and improve the timeliness, accuracy, and usefulness of the agricultural data that informs decisions across American agriculture.

Collecting and sharing dependable agricultural information has been integral to the USDA’s mission since its establishment. Today, USDA data informs crop and livestock estimates, risk-management tools, disaster assistance, and critical business decisions made by farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, researchers, and policymakers, USDA said in a statement.

“America’s farmers and ranchers are the backbone of our food and agricultural system, and USDA should respect their time while delivering the reliable information they need,” Rollins said. “This plan puts farmers first by cutting burdensome red tape, using modern tools, and ensuring producers have a stronger voice in how USDA collects and reports agricultural data. USDA is bringing agricultural data collection into the 21st century while protecting the privacy and trust of the people we serve.”

Earlier this year, Secretary Rollins issued a Request for Information, looking for feedback on the opportunities, challenges, and emerging areas in USDA data.

Additionally, she, and the USDA leadership, held a series of data modernization listening sessions at state fairs and farm shows across the country throughout August to hear directly from hundreds of producers and agricultural stakeholders, the department added.

The feedback and listening sessions resulted in the creation of the USDA Data Modernization Plan and its four pillars:

Modernize the Data Reporting Experience: USDA will expand use of administrative data, improve mobile access to surveys, explore opportunities to use prefilled information where appropriate, and strengthen coordination across the department. These changes will reduce duplicative requests and limit the amount of time producers spend reporting information.

Enhance Acreage and Yield Estimation: USDA will conduct a pilot to evaluate the use of improved satellite imagery, geospatial tools, crop models, and other emerging technologies combined with essential producer-reported information to enhance acreage and yield estimations. USDA will also assess the use of optional field inputs to enhance and ground truth yield estimates and continue advancing yield research through collaboration with agricultural partners and land-grant universities.

Integrate Data and Technology Platforms: USDA will modernize its technology infrastructure, expand secure data-sharing capabilities, and evaluate the responsible use of tools such as artificial intelligence and machine learning. Better integrated systems will improve efficiency, reduce duplication, and allow USDA to produce more timely and useful information.

Expand Trust and Transparency with Producers: USDA will protect producer privacy, clearly explain why information is requested and how it is used, and create additional opportunities for producers to provide feedback. USDA will also improve communication surrounding reports, methodologies, response rates, and data limitations.

“While American agriculture and USDA look vastly different than they did in 1862, the need for timely, accurate, and useful agricultural statistics remains constant,” Kip Tom, USDA’s special advisor for data modernization, said. “This plan brings USDA agencies together, breaks down outdated information silos, and applies modern technology to provide producers and rural communities with better service. By improving how information is collected and shared, we can respond more quickly to challenges facing American agriculture.”

This plan builds on technological advancements already underway across USDA, including satellite-based crop monitoring, geospatial analysis, cloud-based platforms, improved online reporting tools, and more coordinated use of existing administrative data, USDA noted.

The agency will continue to work with partners to assess new methods and improve the scientific foundation of its agricultural statistics.

“USDA’s agricultural statistics are only as strong as the trust and voluntary participation of America’s producers,” Dr. Scott Hutchins, USDA under secretary for research, education, and economics, said. “By combining producer knowledge with sound science and modern technology, USDA can reduce the reporting burden while improving the quality of the information farmers and policymakers rely on. This plan will help ensure American agriculture remains productive and resilient for generations to come.”

The actions under this plan will start being administered immediately, and the USDA will continue working with farmers, ranchers, and agricultural stakeholders throughout the process.

To learn more, view the full USDA Data Modernization Plan here.

translationZh:
华盛顿——在今年的爱荷华州布恩市Farm Progress Show上，美国农业部长Brooke L. Rollins宣布了USDA数据现代化计划，旨在以农民为先，减少生产者不必要的负担，并提高指导美国农业决策的农业数据的及时性、准确性和实用性。

USDA表示，自成立以来，收集和共享可靠的农业信息一直是USDA使命的核心组成部分。如今，USDA数据为作物和畜牧估算、风险管理工具、灾害援助以及农民、牧场主、农业企业、研究人员和政策制定者做出的关键商业决策提供信息支持。

“美国的农民和牧场主是我们食品和农业系统的支柱，USDA应当尊重他们的时间，同时提供他们所需的可靠信息，”Rollins表示。“该计划以农民为先，削减繁琐的官僚程序，使用现代工具，并确保生产者在USDA如何收集和报告农业数据方面拥有更强的发言权。USDA正在将农业数据收集带入21世纪，同时保护我们所服务对象的隐私和信任。”

今年早些时候，Rollins部长发布了一份信息征询书，就USDA数据领域的机遇、挑战和新兴领域征求反馈意见。

此外，她和USDA领导层在整个8月期间在全国各州集市和农业展会上举办了一系列数据现代化意见听取会，直接听取了数百名生产者和农业利益相关者的意见，该部门补充道。

这些反馈和意见听取会促成了USDA数据现代化计划及其四大支柱的创建：

**现代化数据报告体验：** USDA将扩大行政数据的使用，改善调查的移动端访问，探索在适当情况下使用预填信息的可能性，并加强部门内部的协调。这些变化将减少重复请求，限制生产者报告信息所花费的时间。

**增强种植面积与产量估算：** USDA将开展试点，评估改进的卫星影像、地理空间工具、作物模型和其他新兴技术与必要的生产者报告信息相结合，以增强种植面积和产量估算。USDA还将评估可选的田间输入数据的使用，以增强和实地验证产量估算，并继续通过与农业合作伙伴和赠地大学的合作推进产量研究。

**整合数据与技术平台：** USDA将现代化其技术基础设施，扩展安全数据共享能力，并评估人工智能和机器学习等工具的负责任使用。更好的集成系统将提高效率、减少重复，并使USDA能够产出更及时、更有用的信息。

**扩大生产者的信任与透明度：** USDA将保护生产者隐私，清楚解释为何请求信息以及如何使用信息，并为生产者创造更多提供反馈的机会。USDA还将改善围绕报告、方法论、回复率和数据局限性的沟通。

“虽然美国农业和USDA与1862年时已大不相同，但对及时、准确和有用的农业统计数据的需求始终不变，”USDA数据现代化特别顾问Kip Tom表示。“该计划将USDA各机构聚集在一起，打破过时的信息孤岛，并应用现代技术为生产者和农村社区提供更好的服务。通过改善信息的收集和共享方式，我们可以更迅速地应对美国农业面临的挑战。”

USDA指出，该计划建立在USDA已在推进的技术进步基础之上，包括基于卫星的作物监测、地理空间分析、基于云计算的平台、改进的在线报告工具，以及更协调地使用现有行政数据。

该机构将继续与合作伙伴合作，评估新方法并改善其农业统计的科学基础。

“USDA的农业统计数据的力量来自于美国生产者的信任和自愿参与，”USDA研究、教育和经济事务副部长Scott Hutchins博士表示。“通过将生产者知识与可靠科学和现代技术相结合，USDA可以在减少报告负担的同时提高农民和政策制定者所依赖的信息质量。该计划将有助于确保美国农业在未来几代人中保持生产力和韧性。”

该计划下的各项行动将立即开始实施，USDA将在整个过程中继续与农民、牧场主和农业利益相关者合作。

如需了解更多信息，请在此处查看完整的USDA数据现代化计划。
